result.title: SAFE-DRIFT: Data Selection for Supervised Fine-tuning with Controllable Off-Target Drifts
result.summary: We propose SAFE-DRIFT, a data-selection framework for supervised fine-tuning that improves a target capability while controlling unwanted drift in the model's other behaviors. We formalize this as a constrained optimization problem that maximizes alignment with the target gradient, subject to a budget on off-target drift which we quantify using the Fisher information of a reference distribution. Under this objective, the optimal, closed-form update is a damped natural-gradient step that downweights reference-sensitive directions. To estimate these high-dimensional gradients and work within the right geometry, we further derive a scalable algorithm that approximates the Fisher information and the target gradient in a shared low-dimensional subspace and analyze how entanglement of the target and reference task can affect the update. We evaluate SAFE-DRIFT against state-of-the-art data selection methods across diverse domains including coding and medical question answering, yielding competitive target performance while reducing degradation on specified off-target behaviors.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SAFE-DRIFT 监督微调数据筛选框架：把「提升目标能力同时限制其他行为漂移」表述为带 Fisher 信息漂移预算的约束优化，得到对参考分布敏感方向降权的阻尼自然梯度闭式更新，并在共享低维子空间近似 Fisher 与目标梯度以实现可扩展估计，在代码与医学问答等任务上验证。
